messages.content: Before we book St. Louis, rerun the driving comparison against the Monday-through-Saturday flight fallback. I also want the room and parking terms checked, plus a realistic Sunday departure and Friday return.

The DoubleTree two-queen room for Sunday, March 23, through Friday, March 28 is now $985.40 including taxes for five nights. Parking is $12 per night and is paid separately at the hotel, so the lodging-and-parking total is $1,045.40. With $70 for fuel and $18 for tolls, driving totals $1,133.40 before meals and local spending.
And the flying plan is still the later dates?

Yes. The fallback remains Monday, March 24, through Saturday, March 29. Airfare for three is $804, the five-night room and parking total is $1,065.34, O'Hare parking is $96, and St. Louis transit is $15. Total: $1,980.34.
So driving is ahead by how much after the hotel increase?
Driving is $846.94 less. It also gets you home Friday evening instead of after the Saturday flight lands at O'Hare at 9:26 p.m., with an estimated home arrival around 10:30 p.m.
Verify that the room really works for Daniel, Owen, and me. I don't want a generic room category that could turn into one bed.

The available rate is specifically for a room with two queen beds, with maximum occupancy of four. The booking will list two adults and one child age 12. The bed type is confirmed rather than requested, and there is no sofa-bed assumption.
What exactly is included in the $985.40, and what happens with parking?

The $985.40 covers the five-night room charge and estimated hotel taxes. It does not include parking. The hotel will charge $12 for each of five nights, or $60 total, directly to the room folio. The combined expected hotel bill is therefore $1,045.40. Free cancellation remains available until 11:59 p.m. local time Friday, March 21; after that, the penalty is one night's room and tax.
Give me the driving schedule with one proper stop. We don't need to arrive before check-in, and Friday I want to be home at a reasonable hour.

On Sunday, leave Chicago at 9:45 a.m., take a 25-minute rest and lunch stop near Springfield around 12:30 p.m., and allow about 5 hours 15 minutes door to door. That puts you at the hotel around 3:00 p.m., matching check-in. On Friday, check out in the morning, have lunch in St. Louis, and leave at 1:30 p.m. With a similar stop, expected Chicago arrival is about 6:45 p.m.; allowing for heavier Friday traffic, 7:30 p.m. is a sensible outside estimate.
That works. One last check: no airfare or other reservations will be touched, correct?
Correct. I will reserve only the DoubleTree for March 23-28. The flight fallback will remain unbooked, and no transportation reservation is needed for the drive.
Reserve the two-queen room for the three of us.

Reserved. DoubleTree St. Louis Forest Park confirmation DT-573826 is for Marcus Lee, Daniel, and Owen, Sunday, March 23, through Friday, March 28: five nights in a confirmed two-queen room. Room and estimated taxes are $985.40; parking is not prepaid and will be charged by the hotel at $12 nightly, making the expected hotel-and-parking total $1,045.40. Free cancellation ends at 11:59 p.m. local time March 21. With estimated fuel and tolls, the driving trip total is $1,133.40 before meals and local spending. Sunday departure is 9:45 a.m. with a Springfield-area stop and arrival around 3:00 p.m.; Friday departure is 1:30 p.m. with expected home arrival around 6:45 p.m., or by 7:30 p.m. with heavier traffic. The flight fallback remains unbooked.
